title: Roof Replacement in Mission, TX | Edel Roofing & Construction
description: Roof replacement in Mission, TX for original 2000s shingle roofs and storm damage. Full tear off and a written scope before work. Call (956) 422-3335.
lede: Edel Roofing & Construction replaces shingle roofs on Mission homes. We tear off the old roof, check the decking, and give you a written scope before work starts. The estimate is free.

sections.title: Why so many Mission roofs are due now
paras: Mission grew fast in the 2000s. Census survey data (ACS 2020 to 2024) shows about half of the city's 33,400 homes were built in 2000 or later, and the median home was built in 2000. Most of those houses still have the roof they were built with. A shingle roof in the Valley lasts roughly 20 to 25 years, so a big group of Mission homes, including much of Sharyland, is reaching that point at the same time.

An original roof that has made it 20 years is not automatically done. Some still have life left and only need repairs. Others look fine from the street but have brittle shingles and dried out flashing up close. We inspect the whole roof and the decking before we recommend anything, and if repairs would hold, we point you to roof repair in Mission instead.

sections.title: Wind, hail, and rain in Mission
paras: Mission has had its share of storms that end roofs early. On May 31, 2016, a downburst near Palmview and Mission brought winds the NWS estimated at 85 to 95 mph and damaged more than 150 homes and businesses. On April 21, 2023, spotters reported hail up to 2.5 inches in Mission. In July 2020, Hurricane Hanna dropped 14.40 inches of rain on the city, and the NWS reported damage to hundreds of poorly built homes and other buildings, mostly to roofs.

When a storm damages a large part of a 20 year old roof, patching it often costs more over time than replacing it, and the insurance claim may cover much of the new roof. We write down what we find and take photos, so you have something solid to show your insurer.

sections.title: Step by step: a Mission roof replacement

cards.title: 1. Inspection
cards.body: We go on the roof and into the attic, check the decking, and take photos. Free, no obligation.

cards.title: 2. Written scope
cards.body: Shingle line, ventilation, underlayment, price, and timeline, all in writing.

cards.title: 3. Tear off
cards.body: The old roof comes off down to the deck. Bad decking is replaced and noted, not covered over.

cards.title: 4. New roof
cards.body: Synthetic underlayment, new flashing and vents, then CertainTeed, Owens Corning, or GAF shingles.

cards.title: 5. Paperwork
cards.body: You keep the written scope, the photos of your decking, and the final invoice for your records and your insurer.

sections.title: Code and insurance facts for Mission homeowners
paras: Mission builds to the 2024 International Residential Code, and its residential permit application requires an engineered, sealed windstorm plan for new houses. The city has not published a separate rule for reroofing, so if you want to confirm for your address, the Inspections Division is at (956) 580-8691. Work done without a required permit pays a double fee.

Hidalgo County is outside the 14 coastal counties served by the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association, so a Mission roof does not need a TDI windstorm certificate for TWIA. Your regular homeowners policy still matters. The Texas Department of Insurance says insurers cannot refuse or drop you over roof age alone, but some policies pay older roofs at actual cash value.

faqs.q: My house was built around 2002. Do I need a new roof?
faqs.a: Maybe not yet. A roof that age is near the end of its expected life in this climate, but condition matters more than the date. A free inspection tells you whether you have a few years left or should plan for a replacement.

faqs.q: What does a roof replacement cost in Mission?
faqs.a: A full shingle replacement on a typical Mission home generally runs between $8,000 and $18,000. The size and pitch of the roof and the shingle you pick make the difference. The written estimate comes before any work.
CertainTeed, Owens Corning, and GAF. We are the only CertainTeed ShingleMaster PRO in the Rio Grande Valley, which gives you access to stronger warranty coverage on CertainTeed roofs.

faqs.q: Can the storm claim pay for my new roof?
faqs.a: If a covered storm damaged the roof, the claim may pay for much of it, minus your deductible. No contractor can legally waive your deductible in Texas. We document the damage; the claim decision is between you and your insurer.
Most Mission homes are done in one to two days, depending on how big the roof is and the material. Bad weather can add time.

faqs.q: How do I get an estimate in Mission?
faqs.a: Call (956) 422-3335 or book an inspection online. We are about 26 minutes from Mission City Hall, and the estimate is free.
